children: OTTAWA--Canada's official international reserves increased by $368 million in August, the federal finance department said Thursday.
The country's reserves of foreign currencies and other monetary assets totaled $127.41 billion as of Aug. 31, an increase from $127.04 billion the month before.
The government reported no intervention in the foreign-currency market, and there were no gold holdings at the end of the month.
All reserve figures are reported in U.S. dollars.

The finance department said that the amount of Canada bills outstanding rose by $67 million to $1.52 billion as of the end of August. Canada bills are short-term securities sold on the U.S. money market.

At Aug. 31, foreign-currency reserves included securities of $89.37 billion, deposits of $7.74 billion, special drawing rights of $23.92 billion, and a reserve position in the International Monetary Fund of $4.14 billion, the finance department said.

The currency composition of deposits and securities at the end of August included: $64.86 billion U.S. dollars, $16.64 billion euros, $8.77 billion pounds sterling, and $6.84 billion yen.
